title: How to Prevent Lymphedema Complications
content:
Short answer: The main preventable complications of lymphedema are cellulitis, skin breakdown, worsening fibrosis, reduced mobility and loss of daily function. Prevention depends on skin care, compression, movement and early treatment of flares.

Clinically reviewed by Dr Jeremy Sun Mingfa, Plastic, Reconstructive & Lymphedema Surgeon in Singapore. Last reviewed: August 2026. This article is for education only and does not replace personalised medical assessment.

Protect the skin barrier

Small cracks, fungal infection, insect bites or wounds can become entry points for infection. Daily inspection and moisturising are simple but important habits.

Reduce cellulitis risk

  • Treat athlete’s foot and nail infections early.
  • Avoid walking barefoot if the foot is affected.
  • Clean minor cuts promptly and monitor redness.
  • Seek medical care quickly for fever, warmth, spreading redness or sudden swelling.

Prevent progression

Consistent compression, garment refitting, exercise and weight management can reduce worsening heaviness and fibrosis. Waiting until the limb becomes hard and enlarged makes control more difficult.

Review when patterns change

Recurrent cellulitis, increasing compression needs, new pain or loss of function should prompt reassessment. Some patients need imaging or specialist discussion about additional options.

Frequently asked questions

What is the most urgent complication?

Cellulitis can become serious and should be treated promptly.

Can complications be fully prevented?

Not always, but risk can be reduced with consistent care.

When should I ask about surgery?

When conservative care is optimised but infections, swelling or quality-of-life problems continue.

Related surgical guide: If swelling remains persistent despite appropriate conservative care, or if recurrent cellulitis is a major issue, read LVA surgery in Singapore: lymphovenous bypass for lymphedema.
